transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm just... I'm here because of work, mostly. When I try to explain things to my team—like the inventory numbers, or the schedule for the weekend—it just... it doesn't come out right. I start talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm talking about Thursdays, and then the church grill, and... and the way my boss sounded earlier. People just stare at me. Like they have no idea what I'm talking about. So, I guess that's why I'm here.
Over the past week or two, have you noticed your mood being unusually high, elated, or irritable, along with having a lot more energy or needing much less sleep than usual?
No, not really. I sleep fine. My mood is... it's just regular. I haven't been overly happy or anything like that. Just going to work.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?
No. I don't... I don't hear anything like that. Just regular sounds. And I haven't seen anything unusual either. Just normal things.
Do you have any medical conditions—such as a head injury, seizures, thyroid problems, or use of alcohol/drugs—that started around the same time these speech difficulties began?
No. I... no. I haven't been hurt. I don't really drink much, and... no medical things. Just the talking problem. That's all.
How long have you been noticing this trouble with your speech and thoughts jumping around—has it been going on for days, weeks, or several months now?
It's been... I guess about six months now. Just... on the sales floor at work, my explanations get a little jumbled, or I just... stop. So, yeah. Six months.
Have you had any strong beliefs recently—like feeling that people are watching you, talking about you, or trying to control your thoughts—that others don't seem to share?
No, I don't... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. Just... trying to do my job. Nobody's watching me.
Over these past six months, have you noticed yourself pulling away from friends or family, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling less motivated to do everyday tasks?
No, not really. I... I still go to work. Come home. I haven't noticed anything like that. Just sticking to my normal routine, I guess.
Have you or others noticed unusual behaviors, like unpredictable actions, odd movements, or periods where you seem to freeze up or not respond, alongside the speech difficulties?

I don't know if it's unusual, but... sometimes on the sales floor, I catch myself just pacing the same aisle. Straightening the same row of batteries, over and over. Or... I'll just be standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand. The associates will be waiting for me to tell them what to do, and I'm just standing there. So... yeah. I guess that happens sometimes.

Compared to six months ago, have you noticed any change in how well you're able to do your job or handle daily responsibilities—like needing more help, making more mistakes, or falling behind on tasks you used to manage easily?

I suppose things are... a bit harder. They don't let me run the weekend shifts anymore. Too busy, I guess. My boss... he gave me a review. Said I might be suspended if I don't get it together. And at home... my wife just does things I used to do. Social things, mostly. People were acting... uncomfortable around me. So she just handles it now.
Have you or your wife noticed that your facial expressions or tone of voice have become more flat or less emotional than before, even in situations where you'd normally show more feeling?
I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. My wife... she hasn't said anything about my face or my voice. I think I sound the same as I always do.

latest_inference.note: The 6-month duration of disorganized speech, functional decline (job demotion, social withdrawal handled by spouse), and catatonic-like behaviors (freezing, repetitive purposeless actions) support schizophrenia. Absence of mood episode, hallucinations, delusions, or substance/medical cause reduces likelihood of other psychosis types, and the symptom duration/functional impairment now exceeds the criteria for unspecified psychosis (F29), narrowing the diagnosis to schizophrenia.
